newsitem.title: USA: Sara Lee sees record results for rest of FY97.
newsitem.headline: Sara Lee sees record results for rest of FY97.

text.p: Sara Lee Corp, which reported record results for the third quarter ended March 29, said Thursday it expects record results for the remainder of fiscal 1997.

"We are pleased to have posted increased sales and earnings as well as improved operating margins for the third quarter (ended March 29) of fiscal 1997, and our expectations are to continue to report record results for the remainder of the 1997 fiscal year," John Bryan, chairman, said in a statement.
Sara Lee today reported net income for the third quarter of $0.41 a share, up from $0.37 a year ago, and net sales of $4.6 billion, up from $4.4 billion.

"Sara Lee Corp also enjoyed an increased rate of unit volume growth in this most recent period as overall corporate unit sales, excluding the impact of acquisitions, rose four percent during the third quarter," Bryan said. "Both our food and non-food businesses showed good unit gains, with particularly strong results in our foodservice operations, European roasted coffee, and U.S. hosiery and knit product divisions."

Sara Lee said packaged meats and bakery sales in the third quarter rose 16.4 percent to $1.79 billion, and operating income increased 11.2 percent to $99 million. These results were aided by base business growth and the acquisition of the French processed meats company Aoste.

Coffee and grocery sales dropped 1.3 percent in the third quarter to $684 million, and opreating income declined 2.1 percent to $99 million. Sara Lee said the stronger dollar relative to European currencies hurt translated results. In local currency terms, sales rose significantly, with double-digit profit growth during the quarter, it added.
Unit volumes for roasted coffee, excluding acquisitions, were up 11 percent in the quarter.

Sara Lee said household and body care third quarter sales dropped 3.4 percent to $448 million, while operating income gained 5.1 percent to $49 million. It said results benefited from increased profitability in the core household and body care product categories, which include shoe care, body care and insecticides, and higher sales from the direct selling division.
Personal products sales dropped 1.1 percent to $1.73 billion, while operating income rose 10.9 percent to $158 million.

Unit volumes for worldwide legwear rose two percent in the quarter, reflecting flat unit volumes for sheer hosiery and a nine percent increase in unit sales for socks. For the first time in more than two years, sheer hosiery units were up in the United States on the strength of gains at both Hanes and L'eggs, it added.
Worldwide knit product unit sales rose seven percent in the quarter, and intimate apparel unit volumes gained two percent on a global basis.
